ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High macro-level contrast characterized by approximately 75% high-intensity white pixels in the interior fluke regions and 25% low-intensity dark pixels concentrated at the margins and linear features.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous low-intensity banding follows the entire trailing edge boundary. High-contrast vertical streaks are mapped heavily onto the right lobe medial-to-distal section. Isolated dark mottling is localized on the lower-left central quadrant.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped central depression with a calculated interior pixel angle of approximately 48 degrees and a deep bounding-box penetration relative to the lobe peak.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude serrations across the entire trailing edge boundary. Significant jagged pixel-valleys (notches) are located on the inner-left trailing edge and outer-right trailing edge.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly concave sweep trajectory extending from the median notch to the distal tips of both lobes.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized clusters of circular low-intensity pixel groups (suggestive of barnacle scarring) are visible on the distal tip of the right lobe and along the upper-left trailing margin.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple parallel, vertically-oriented dark linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) are mapped across the right lobe, oriented perpendicular to the trailing edge.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive irregular tissue loss and fragmentation along the trailing edge resulting in a non-uniform, ragged silhouette. Distinct bluntness visible on the left tip compared to the more acute right tip.
other_distinctive_markers: A small, high-intensity white 'island' or focal spot is embedded within the dark pigmentation zone near the right lobe tip.
